prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, full body shot. ONE woman standing.

a deep ebony-brown complexion, early 20s goddess, violin hip hourglass physique THE MOST EXTREME PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE beyond all anatomy limits — an extraordinarily curvaceous woman, far beyond any real person; a sharply cinched waist rises out of hips that sweep outward in a single smooth violin-shaped curve, the hips and thick rounded thighs flaring many times wider than the waist and dominating her silhouette from the front and side, a firm high rounded rear, a full round bust balancing the curve above; the line from waist to hip to thigh is one long unbroken curve; her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other, sculpted updo copper red hair — her skin is her only outfit. Her bare skin below the jaw is painted in Mexican Talavera ceramic — a glossy white tin glaze with cobalt blue and marigold medallions, wide cobalt bands following every deep crease and curving around the hips like contour lines, dense medallion scrollwork filling the space between every band; the paint is pigment sitting on living skin and covers her shoulders, arms, chest, midriff, hips and legs down to her ankles, her face left as real unpainted skin with the pattern fading out at the neck. Real photographic skin shows through the artwork across her whole body, with visible pores, fine peach-fuzz hairs, a light scatter of faint freckles and small moles, the paint and ink sitting on living skin and her skin tone running naturally under it. Pose: strong hip pop left, both hands pressing outer hips outward arching back to extreme, her legs fully in view — most extreme violin hip hourglass silhouette ever displayed.
Footwear: heels of the most absurdly extreme height imaginable, pointed platform stiletto pumps made of glossy bronze leather, each with a razor-thin tapered heel a full forty inches tall and a twelve-inch hidden front platform, her feet arched fully vertical on the very tips of her toes like a dancer on pointe, her legs stretched impossibly long and her whole body lifted far above the ground on them as if standing on stilts.
Nails: the longest nails physically imaginable, almond nails each as long as her forearm is wide, in bronze lacquer with a high polish.
Jewelry: a pair of large chandelier earrings of tin and blackened iron as her only jewelry, her neck, collarbones, chest, arms, wrists and fingers plain bare skin.
Face: her face is bare of any garment — real living flesh with real pores, a soft sheen of natural oils and bright real catchlights, the face of a real Black woman with strong, striking features, a broad nose and full lips, an unmistakably feminine face with a calm, composed expression, makeup: pushed to the absolute extreme, thick opaque layers piled on: an opaque thick white eyeshadow smeared from the lash line up to the brows, thick white paint under the lower lashes, a very wide bright turquoise liner flaring far past the outer corners, extremely long clumped false lashes top and bottom, opaque glossy white lips.

Background: a mirrored cube room with mirrors on all four walls, the ceiling and a glossy black floor, thin hot-pink neon LED strips running along every corner so the pink lines multiply into an endless glowing lattice in all directions, her figure repeated in the lattice from every side, the whole floor clearly visible and in focus, lit by the pink neon and soft light with gentle shadows. ONE woman only. Full-length wide shot from a moderate distance with the camera at waist height, the whole figure from the soles of her shoes to the top of her head completely visible, the towering heels clearly separating the shoes from the floor. This is one single photograph taken with one camera at one moment, the reflections being part of that same photograph, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/5.6, realistic photographic grain, a real photograph. Portrait 2:3 aspect ratio.
